name: Sea Turtle Grants Program (Florida)
summary: Annual competitive grants, funded by Florida's sea turtle licence plate, for sea turtle research, conservation and education projects in Florida, including nesting-beach protection. Florida local governments, non-profits and research institutions apply.

steps: Digital application and mailed signed hard copy
FWCC technical review, research proposals only

eligibility.rule: Is based in Florida and actively participates in marine turtle activities within Florida
Project preserves Florida marine turtles, meets recovery-plan tasks, FWCC programme goals and s.370.12(1)(c)
Funds are not used for fundraising or membership materials, or for any litigation
Submits no more than four grant applications per funding cycle

documents: Digital NMFS Permit copy, if applicable
Letter of endorsement, if the Project Manager lacks authority
Letter of support from a cooperating entity, if applicable
Education or conservation item description page, if applicable
Mock-up, draft design or draft text for proposed materials or displays, if applicable
Sample of existing educational item, if requesting a reprint
Research proposal with methods and data analysis, if research
C.V. or resume for each research project person, if research

effort.quote: Complete Digital Grant Applications must be submitted online by no later than 5:00 pm on Friday, November 6, 2026
One (1) original printed (hard copy) Grant Application with signed Cover Sheet must be mailed to the following address and postmarked by 5:00 pm on Friday, November 6, 2026
STC will send complete applications for research proposals to FWCC staff for review.
Applications shall be selected for funding by the Sea Turtle Grant Committee (Committee).

eligibility.quote: Florida Coastal Local Governments, Florida-based Non-Profit Organizations, and Florida-based Education and Research Institutions that actively participate in marine turtle research, conservation, and educational activities within the state of Florida are eligible to apply for and receive grant funds.

Funds can be requested for projects in one of three categories (conservation, education or research) that clearly add to the preservation of Florida’s marine turtles; that accomplish tasks included in the current recovery plans for marine turtles; that address the goals of the FWCC’s Marine Turtle Protection Program; and that are consistent with subsection 370.12 (1) (c), Florida Statutes.
grant funds may not be used for materials that contain fundraising or membership development language, or to support any type of litigation.
A maximum of four (4) Grant Applications for funding may be submitted during each funding cycle by an eligible organization/institution/agency.

documents.quote: Copy of current MTP Permit (if applicable) Digital only copy NMFS Permit, please don't print out your NMFS Permit (if applicable)
a letter of endorsement signed by an Authorized Representative of the listed organization must be included after the Cover Sheet
cooperation with, or involvement of, another entity, please provide a letter of support from that entity.
Education & Conservation description page for each item requested
Please provide a quote for all equipment requests.
Please provide a mock-up, draft design or draft text of any proposed materials or displays. If you are requesting a reprint of educational materials, please include a sample of the existing item(s).

Research Grant Applications should include a separate research proposal with introduction, objectives, detailed methods (including data analysis), and a C.V. or resume (2 pages or less) for each person involved in the proposed project.
